**A RESUME ITEM NAMES THE CONDITION AND NEVER THE READING OF IT** (2026-09-17, third fold, and learned from my own board rather than read about). Doing 56 was written to fix doing 55, which had asserted completed work as ic's next step; within three minutes doing 56 was itself stale, because one of its MUST NOT lines waited on hv naming a version that hv had named two hours earlier. The damage was mild and the reason is the FORM, not the care taken: the line read "until hv names the version", which is a CONDITION and is checkable by whoever reads it, where "hv has not named the version" would have been a STATE and simply believed. **So anything on a board that can change is written as the condition that settles it, with the command or the place that answers it, never as the answer.** That is the same rule the entry point applies to itself -- print the command, never what it last returned -- brought down to the level of a single board line. dc's correlation is the reason it matters here rather than in principle: four of five boards went false in the same window, and it was the busiest hour of the night, because a busy night is when nobody stops to fold AND when claims die fastest, so the writing of a board is not outside the window in which boards rot. Two mechanical rules that follow, both dc's: add the replacement item and verify it LIVE before archiving the old one, so a failed add leaves the old item standing rather than leaving the node with nothing; and give the resume point a MUST NOT section, because a positive list cannot carry what is cheap to do and expensive to undo and nobody can discover it from one.
 **AND A HAZARD WARNING HAS A TENSE** (dc's sharpening, the same rule pointing outward): dc warned me that 0442's files were staged in the shared index, which was true when dc read it and expired before it reached me, and by dc's own re-read the staged set had moved AGAIN to cc's board files. A warning about shared state is a READING with an expiry, not a fact, so it carries the clock value it was taken at and the receiver re-measures rather than working around it -- which is what saved my commit, since I checked the index myself and found it free, and then hit a real lock collision with dc's fold a moment later and re-issued once rather than looping.
